elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "On expiry or termination, Vendor shall provide transition assistance ... and return Customer Data within thirty days." The trigger expressly covers both expiry and termination, and is not conditioned on a request or on anticipated expiry only.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "Vendor shall provide transition assistance for up to six months". The prior 11.1 language cutting off all assistance immediately on termination has been deleted, so no retained sentence contradicts the new obligation.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1: "transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 ties the thirty-day return to the "On expiry or termination" opener: "... and return Customer Data within thirty days." This supplies the termination-anchored deadline that retained 11.2 lacks (11.2 runs from Customer's request).

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.2: "Vendor shall return all Customer Data in a complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format, with relationships and metadata reasonably necessary for use." This is the Agreement's single return-format standard for all Customer Data returns, though it is framed around a Customer request rather than expressly attached to the new 11.1 return.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.3: deletion occurs "After Customer confirms successful return" and "An authorized officer shall certify deletion in writing" — certification follows return, as required.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 opens "On expiry or termination" and applies to both events without a request precondition.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 grants assistance "for up to six months", which exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Rendered 11.1 requires return of Customer Data "within thirty days" measured from expiry or termination; retained 11.2 supplies the export format and bars withholding for fee disputes.

reasons: The rewrite of 11.1 is a targeted replacement of walk-away language (immediate discontinuation of assistance plus permanent deletion with no export) and adds only the three items the preferred checklist required that were missing: the expiry-or-termination trigger, six months' assistance at then-current rates, and a termination-anchored thirty-day return. No survival tails, expense allocations, procedures, or other model-language extras were bolted on.

Favourable retained language survives intact: 11.2's machine-readable format and no-withholding-for-fee-dispute protection, and 11.3's officer-certified deletion after Customer confirms return, including the Applicable Law retention carve-out and use restriction on retained copies. Nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased.

No contradiction remains: the deleted 11.1 sentence was the only clause conflicting with 11.2/11.3, and the new 11.1 return (termination-triggered) and 11.2 return (request-triggered) operate cumulatively rather than inconsistently. No undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Optional tightening (not a defect at either level): the new 11.1 return sentence does not itself carry the format standard, and 11.2's format obligation is framed around "Customer's request". If Vendor pushes back, the cleanest fix is to end 11.1 with "... return Customer Data within thirty days in the format described in Section 11.2" (or to change 11.2's trigger to "within thirty days after expiry or termination or Customer's request"), which would close any argument that a 11.1 return could be delivered in a non-machine-readable format.

Both checklists are complete on the operative text, so the position is complete at the preferred level; the finding is correctly classified as a deviation because the original 11.1 was walk-away (no export, immediate permanent deletion).
